strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime can run one already admitted LLM provider failure retry task through the existing task.run provider, network, sensitive-prompt, and AccessNetwork gates.
Headless callers can continue from the M20.1 retry-task route into one bounded provider retry execution without switching to direct task.run orchestration.

Retry execution decisions and provider failures remain replayable ledger facts without raw prompts, provider responses, request bodies, file content, command output, environment values, secrets, or raw paths.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances llm_provider_execution with supporting headless_autonomous_development and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.continue_once accepts a bounded llm_provider_failure_retry_run_target and runs exactly one already admitted retry task through existing task.run execution authority.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M20.1 only admitted a retry task and returned a route; external controllers still had to switch protocols to task.run, losing headless stale-progress validation and continuation replay for the execution step.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Provider failures remain only half recoverable in the headless loop: the runtime can create retry tasks but cannot execute them as part of the replay-safe headless continuation contract.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M19.2 carried context budgets into ordinary headless execution, M19.3 drove bounded headless sessions, and M20.1 admitted provider retry tasks; M20.2 runs the admitted provider retry task.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.continue_once request/result contract is extended; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The run target is an execution request and returns existing TaskRunResult evidence, not a new report/history/readiness surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: After stale-progress validation, the runtime revalidates retry provenance, checks explicit run authorization, delegates to existing task.run, records one headless decision, and replays the continuation without duplicate execution.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can complete the next provider recovery step using a single deterministic headless contract and can distinguish stale progress, invalid targets, permission denial, execution result, and replay.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the core M20 vertical after M20.1 by converting provider retry routing into bounded provider retry execution under Rust runtime authority.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M20.2 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm actual headless provider retry execution behavior, replay safety, and reuse of Rust-owned task.run gates.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts llm_provider_failure_retry_run_target without adding a new RPC
valid provider retry run target executes exactly one admitted retry task through existing task.run
same continuation_id replays the bounded execution decision without duplicate TaskRunning, provider request, provider failure, or headless execution decision events
stale progress rejects before retry task execution or decision mutation
invalid authorization, stale failure fingerprint, invalid target task/run, context_budget, max_steps, and incompatible recovery-field combinations reject before execution
AccessNetwork denial is surfaced through existing task.run provider failure evidence without sending provider requests

ledger and RPC results contain bounded identifiers/outcomes only and no raw prompt, provider response, request body, file content, stdout, stderr, command, environment, secret, absolute path, or canonical path
VSIX protocol validators accept valid provider retry run target params and reject raw-data-bearing or unauthorized payloads

tests: VSIX headless provider retry run target validator cases

next_phase_candidate_notes: After M20.2 merge, evaluate M20 closeout or a distinct recovery capability such as bounded provider retry result routing into follow-up planning. Reject provider retry reports, histories, readiness wrappers, and automatic provider calls.
